chosen.premise: Abra can teleport safely while asleep, but wakes up panicking because it has no idea where it landed.
chosen.hook: Abra’s safest escape creates a terrifying morning surprise.
chosen.visualIdea: Abra teleports in its sleep, opens its eyes in a strange place, and panics.
chosen.note: A sharply Abra-specific contradiction: sleeping makes escape possible, but the successful teleport leaves Abra disoriented and panicked on waking. The emotional beat is clear and easy to stage.

candidates.premise: Abra can teleport safely while asleep, but wakes up panicking because it has no idea where it landed.

candidates.visualIdea: Abra teleports in its sleep, opens its eyes in a strange place, and panics.

candidates.premise: The deeper Abra sleeps, the farther its unconscious Teleports can carry it.
candidates.hook: The deeper Abra sleeps, the farther it can accidentally go.
candidates.visualIdea: Use a sleep-depth meter as Abra’s teleport distance grows from nearby to far away.
candidates.note: A precise, surprising rule with an obvious visual meter. It relies on a single Pokédex statement, but that statement directly supports the premise.

candidates.premise: When Abra Teleports randomly, observers may see an illusion that it created copies of itself.
candidates.hook: Abra can look like it multiplied without creating a single copy.
candidates.visualIdea: Abra blinks unpredictably across the screen until several apparent copies fill the frame.
candidates.note: The illusion of multiplication is well supported and visually strong, but it is more of a familiar teleportation trick than the uniquely strange sleep-and-panic behavior.

candidates.premise: Abra’s dreams affect the psychic powers it wields, making sleep part of its power system.
candidates.hook: For Abra, dreaming is basically training.
candidates.visualIdea: Different dream scenes transform into different psychic effects around sleeping Abra.
candidates.note: Directly supported by the Sword entry and visually adaptable, though the idea is slightly less sharply defined than the strongest behavioral contradictions.

candidates.premise: During its 18-hour sleep, Abra changes location once every hour using Teleport.
candidates.hook: Abra may wake up 18 places away from where it fell asleep.
candidates.visualIdea: A clock advances hour by hour while sleeping Abra blinks between 18 different locations.
candidates.note: The hourly relocation is concrete and highly visual, but the hook overreaches: changing location once per hour does not establish 18 distinct destinations or that Abra wakes 18 places away.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; the chosen premise is already strong. Any alternative would need an equally specific contradiction or rule, direct Pokédex support, and a clearer visual payoff without overstating what the text says.
